newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to put labels on beef to reassure customers.
newsitem.headline: EU to put labels on beef to reassure customers.

text.p: European Union farm ministers, in a bid to restore consumer confidence after the mad cow disease crisis, agreed on Wednesday that from 2000, beef sold in shops will have to carry a label showing where it comes from, a Commission spokesman said.

The decision was agreed unanimously on the third day of ministerial talks after the Dutch EU Presidency won British and Italian support by inserting an opt-out clause allowing a member state to apply the system on a voluntary basis on its territory.
"They all agreed a third compromise," the spokesman said.

Unanimity was required after ministers rejected a European Commission proposal that would have given the European Parliament power to decide jointly the creation of EU cattle identification and beef labelling systems.
Britain had been worried that indicating where cattle were born, raised and slaughtered would deter continental buyers and infringe trade in the single EU market.
Italy, which imports a lot of calves from eastern Europe, was concerned that providing such information would create an adverse reaction among Italian consumers.
Labelling of beef imports from countries outside the EU would be subject to negotiation and would have to respect World Trade Organisation free trade rules
